answer: Each newcomer must finish a timed fusee they cannot share. An applicant posts 4.15 POA and books an 8-minute lathe among 22 clock bays. They coat a 7.2 g yarrow-oil umber enamel on the cone, then shine a 17-bit seed-bound lamp through a standing prism so the workshop photogate logs the cone's flare in seconds 16-40. 136 clones would freeze 564.4 POA and need 136 exclusive bays. Graders replay the bay draw from the seed, match the flare bits, and weigh the enamel to 0.05 g. A reused lathe, missed flare, or bit clash slashes 50% and benches that bay for 4 epochs.
